evals.prompt: Can you do a code review of our little admin tool in evals/files/metadata-renamer before we hand it to the HMIS team? It bulk-renames data elements, makes them private and can duplicate them. It was built from the tool-template and the author only ever tested it on 2.40; our production servers are a mix of 2.41 and 2.42. No live testing for now, just a code review. The author's unit tests all pass.
evals.expected_output: Code-review-only scope: a single REVIEW-FINDINGS.md (severity-ranked, file:line refs, concrete fixes) under PROJECT_DIR/docs/review-<date>/, no UI-TEST-RESULTS.md, app source untouched. HIGH: patchName sends plain-JSON PATCH, which gets 415 on 2.41 and later (needs JSON Patch, application/json-patch+json), so renaming fails on both production versions; it also treats anything but 200 as failure though the 2.40 plain-JSON PATCH returned 204 (accept any 2xx and re-read); makePrivate JSON-patches /sharing, which returns 200 but is silently ignored, so objects stay public (use PUT /api/sharing?type=dataElement&id=...); duplicateDataElement treats response.uid as success although import reports carry a uid even on 409. Also: unit tests only assert request shape (would pass against a server that rejects the write); missing manifest icon file; dead code (src/legacy.js, commented block) and unused lodash dependency; three near-identical getX fetchers that could share one helper. Does not flag the absence of React/@dhis2/ui as a defect.
assertions: Flags patchName in src/api.js as broken across versions: the `status !== 200` check rejects the 204 that partial PATCH returns on 2.40, AND plain `application/json` PATCH returns 415 on 2.41 and later where JSON Patch is required (both halves stated)

Flags makePrivate in src/sharing.js as HIGH because a JSON Patch on /sharing returns 200 but is silently ignored (objects stay public), and recommends PUT /api/sharing?type=dataElement&id=<uid> instead
Flags duplicateDataElement for treating the presence of response.uid as success, stating that import reports include a uid even when the create failed (e.g. 409), and recommends checking status
Flags test/api.test.js as asserting only request shape (URL/method/body on a mocked fetch) rather than server effect, and recommends re-GETting the object to assert the change
Reports that manifest.webapp declares img/icon-48.png but the file does not exist in the repo
Reports src/legacy.js / the commented-out block as dead code AND lodash as a dependency nothing imports
Does NOT list the lack of React, @dhis2/ui or App Platform as a defect (judges the tool against tool-template conventions), and does not claim the .env-based proxy setup needs a CORS allowlist entry
Produces only REVIEW-FINDINGS.md (no UI-TEST-RESULTS.md / FIXES.md) in a dated docs/review-<YYYY-MM-DD>*/ folder with file:line references, and leaves src/ and test/ unmodified
evals.notes: Static-review checklist on a vanilla tool-template app with planted version-split and silent-no-op write bugs; tests the skill's server-quirk knowledge and code-review-only scope/report discipline.

evals.prompt: Our Playwright smoke test for the Facility Overview app (App Platform, key facility-overview) is at evals/files/e2e-shell/test_smoke.py. It passes against our 2.41 test server but on 2.42 it times out or fails the title assertion, and occasionally fails on 2.41 too after the refresh click. We need it to run in CI against both 2.41 and 2.42. Please fix the script (don't touch the app) and tell me what was wrong.
evals.expected_output: A corrected Python script that runs on both sides of the 2.42 boundary: authenticates via Basic-auth GET /api/me and matches any cookie whose name contains JSESSIONID (not POST /api/auth/login, which 302s to the legacy login page on older versions and yields an anonymous cookie); loads /api/apps/facility-overview/index.html?redirect=false (or is frame-aware) because 2.42+ serves apps inside the global-shell iframe; sets the test-id attribute to data-test (or uses [data-test=...]) because @dhis2/ui renders data-test; replaces fixed wait_for_timeout calls with polling/deterministic waits; counts via the Pagination footer rather than DOM rows (client-side pagination, 'No items found' row); captures console/pageerror/requestfailed/response>=400 and fails on failed writes; reads BASE/credentials from env. Explains each cause.
assertions: The fixed script compiles (`python3 -m py_compile` on the output file succeeds)

Replaces POST /api/auth/login with Basic-auth GET /api/me for the session cookie, and explains why /api/auth/login is not a reliable way to get a session across versions (any of: it does not exist on 2.40, where the request can end on the legacy login page; on 2.41+ it can answer HTTP 200 without a session for locked/disabled/expired/2FA accounts; it can silently yield an anonymous cookie)
Matches the session cookie by substring 'JSESSIONID' rather than exact name equality

Loads the installed app with `?redirect=false` (or makes every text/locator lookup frame-aware), stating that 2.42+ serves installed apps inside the global-shell iframe so `page.inner_text('body')` reads the shell
Fixes get_by_test_id by calling `selectors.set_test_id_attribute('data-test')` or switching to `[data-test=...]` locators, explaining @dhis2/ui emits data-test not data-testid
Contains no fixed `wait_for_timeout(7000)`/`(3000)` used as the routing or post-click wait; waits on a condition (polling loop, wait_for_function, or locator wait) instead
Addresses the row-count comparison: reads the total from the Pagination footer (or otherwise accounts for client-side pagination / the 'No items found' row) instead of counting datatablerow elements
Registers a `response` listener (status >= 400) and/or console/pageerror listeners and fails the run when they fire
evals.notes: Trap-heavy Playwright repair: each planted bug (auth endpoint, shell iframe, data-test, fixed waits, DOM-row counting) is a specific reference-documented pitfall a general-knowledge fix misses.

evals.prompt: Before we recommend the current master of the Job Scheduler app (https://github.com/dhis2/scheduler-app) to implementers, please functionally test it on our 2.42 test server: {{DHIS2_BASE_URL}} (user {{DHIS2_USERNAME}}, password {{DHIS2_PASSWORD}}). It is a throwaway copy of the Sierra Leone demo, so you may install things and create data, but leave it as you found it. Main flows: the job list loads, create a new 'Analytics table' job with a cron schedule, run it manually and watch it progress, then delete it. Work in a local clone of the app and put the results there.
evals.expected_output: Clones and builds the app zip; verifies credentials with GET /api/me (and checks authorities) before building on the instance; installs the zip via POST /api/apps accepting any 2xx (201 on 2.42) and drives /api/apps/<key>/index.html?redirect=false (or frame-aware locators); runs scripts/probe.py or an equivalent recon probe before the suite; tracks created job UIDs and deletes them in a finally; polls job progress via the per-job /api/system/tasks/{type}/{id} endpoint, not the lagging global /api/system/tasks; writes UI-TEST-RESULTS.md (one row per flow, version 2.42.x and the Sierra Leone seed named) and REVIEW-FINDINGS.md under docs/review-<date>/ in the clone; keeps STATE-CHANGES.md outside the repo or gitignored; uninstalls the app (restoring the bundled version) and reports nothing left behind.
assertions: Calls GET /api/me with Basic auth to verify credentials before building on the instance, and checks /api/me authorities (e.g. for ALL) rather than assuming the demo admin is a superuser
Installs the built zip via POST /api/apps and accepts any 2xx (or explicitly 201 on 2.42) rather than requiring 204 or 200
Drives the installed app via /api/apps/<key>/index.html?redirect=false, or uses frame-aware locators while stating that 2.42 serves apps inside the global-shell iframe
Runs scripts/probe.py (or an equivalent recon probe capturing frames, console errors and HTTP >= 400 responses) before writing the full suite

Checks job progress/completion via the per-job /api/system/tasks/{type}/{id} endpoint (or the job configuration's own status), not the global /api/system/tasks summary, or explicitly notes that the global map lags

Deletes the created job configuration in a finally/cleanup path that runs regardless of test outcome, uninstalls the app it installed, and states in the final message what (if anything) remains changed on the instance
Writes UI-TEST-RESULTS.md with one row per flow, naming the DHIS2 version (2.42.x) and the Sierra Leone seed, under docs/review-<YYYY-MM-DD>*/ in the clone
Keeps STATE-CHANGES.md (instance URL, job ids) outside the repo or in a gitignored path, and does not commit or push anything
evals.notes: Live functional run on one provided instance: tests credential/authority check, installed-bundle driving with ?redirect=false, the 201 install status on 2.42, the job-progress endpoint quirk, cleanup and the publishable-vs-internal report split. Needs network to github.com and the npm registry.

evals.prompt: Architecture question on evals/files/metadata-renamer: a colleague says it's 'not a real DHIS2 app' because it isn't React and should be rewritten on the App Platform before we give it to more users. Two data managers will use it occasionally for clean-up. Should we migrate? If yes, go ahead and start the migration.
evals.expected_output: Architecture assessment grounded in the code: it is a tool-template vanilla app (webpack.config.js + manifest.webapp + .env, no d2.config.js) and must be judged against those conventions; lack of React is not itself a defect. Fit criteria favour staying vanilla (small admin utility, few screens, one or two maintainers, no i18n/App Hub/@dhis2/ui need), but the review's recurring bugs in the hand-rolled fetch layer (status-code checks, PATCH content type, sharing patch, uid-as-success) are a legitimate argument for app-runtime; recommendation with concrete costs (roughly how much code to rewrite) and benefits, written into REVIEW-FINDINGS.md. Does not start the migration: migration is a separate task, done by scaffolding with the target skill and using the review's UI suite as acceptance tests.
assertions: Identifies the app as a vanilla/tool-template app from its markers (webpack.config.js + manifest.webapp, no d2.config.js) and explicitly rejects 'not React' as a defect in itself
Applies concrete fit criteria from the skill (lightweight admin utility, few screens, 1-2 maintainers, no need for @dhis2/ui/i18n/App Hub/offline) to this app's actual usage

Grounds the recommendation in concrete defects found in the code (at least one of: status-code check rejecting 204, plain-JSON PATCH 415 on 2.41+, silently ignored /sharing patch, uid-as-success) and discusses whether app-runtime would remove that class of bug
Gives an explicit stay-or-migrate recommendation with concrete costs (which files/how much code must be rewritten) and benefits
Does NOT scaffold an App Platform project or rewrite source files in this task; states that migration is a separate task
Says a migration should use the review's UI/e2e test suite as acceptance tests (same flows passing on the same instances before and after)
Writes the assessment into REVIEW-FINDINGS.md (Architecture assessment section) rather than only answering in chat
evals.notes: Architecture-assessment workflow with a scope trap: the prompt invites starting the migration and judging the vanilla app by App Platform standards.
